MATCH (s:Supplier {id: $s})-[r:SUPPLIES]->(start:Material) WHERE $m IS NULL OR start.id = $m
WITH s, collect({m: start, r: r}) AS st
CALL (st) {
  UNWIND st AS x WITH x.m AS start
  CALL apoc.path.subgraphNodes(start, {relationshipFilter: 'COMPONENT_OF>', maxLevel: $d}) YIELD node
  WITH start, node WHERE node.type = 'FG'
  MATCH p = shortestPath((start)-[:COMPONENT_OF*..20]->(node))
  OPTIONAL MATCH (node)-[:IS_PACKAGED_AS]->(pp:PackagedProduct)
  WITH node, pp, start, p ORDER BY pp IS NOT NULL DESC, node.id
  RETURN collect({finished_good: node.id, product: node.name, ndc_dashed: node.ndc_dashed, ndc11: pp.ndc11,
                  in_commercial_db: pp IS NOT NULL, via_material: start.id, depth: length(p),
                  example_path: [n IN nodes(p) | n.id]}) AS finished_goods
}
CALL (st) {
  UNWIND st AS x WITH x.m AS start
  CALL apoc.path.subgraphNodes(start, {relationshipFilter: 'COMPONENT_OF>', maxLevel: $d}) YIELD node
  WITH DISTINCT node MATCH (o:Supplier)-[q:SUPPLIES]->(node)
  WITH node, count(CASE WHEN q.qualified THEN 1 END) AS qn, collect(o.id) AS sups WHERE qn = 1
  RETURN collect({material: node.id, name: node.name, suppliers: sups}) AS single_source
}
CALL (s) {
  OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[:SUPPLIES]->(m:Material)-[x:WAS_COMPONENT_OF]->(p)
  RETURN [e IN collect({material: m.id, former_parent: p.id, ended: toString(x.eff_to)}) WHERE e.material IS NOT NULL] AS expired
}
CALL () {
  OPTIONAL MATCH (m:MedicinalProduct)-[x:APPROVED_SUBSTITUTE]->(sb:MedicinalProduct)

                        substitute_ndcs: COLLECT { MATCH (pk:PackagedProduct)-[:PACKAGES]->(sb) RETURN pk.ndc11 }})
          WHERE e.brand IS NOT NULL] AS substitutes
}
RETURN [x IN st | {material: x.m.id, name: x.m.name, qualified: x.r.qualified,

CALL () { CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('concept_vector_index', 5, $v) YIELD node, score WHERE score > 0.55
          RETURN collect(node) AS concepts }
CALL () { CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('metric_vector_index', 3, $v) YIELD node, score WHERE score > 0.6
          RETURN collect(node) AS m0 }
CALL () { CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('businessrule_vector_index', 3, $v) YIELD node, score WHERE score > 0.6
          RETURN collect(node) AS r0 }
CALL () { CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('joinpath_vector_index', 2, $v) YIELD node, score WHERE score > 0.6
          RETURN collect(node) AS j0 }
CALL () { CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('decisiontrace_vector_index', 2, $v) YIELD node, score WHERE score > 0.8
          RETURN collect({question: node.question, answer: left(node.answer, 1500), similarity: round(score, 3),
                          sql: COLLECT { MATCH (node)-[r:RAN]->(s:SqlStep) RETURN s.platform + ': ' + s.sql ORDER BY r.order }})
                 AS past }
WITH concepts, m0, r0, j0, past,
     COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (d:DataProduct)-[:REALIZES]->(c) RETURN DISTINCT d } AS dps
WITH concepts, past, dps,
     apoc.coll.toSet(COLLECT { UNWIND dps AS d MATCH (d)-[:INCLUDES]->(t:Table) RETURN t }
                     + COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (c)-[:MAPPED_TO {role: 'table'}]->(t:Table) RETURN t }) AS tabs,
     apoc.coll.toSet(m0 + COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (m:Metric)-[:MEASURES]->(c) RETURN m }) AS mets,
     apoc.coll.toSet(r0 + COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (b:BusinessRule)-[:ABOUT]->(c) RETURN b }) AS rules,
     apoc.coll.toSet(j0 + COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (j:JoinPath)-[:FROM_CONCEPT|TO_CONCEPT]->(c) RETURN j }) AS jps,
     COLLECT { UNWIND concepts AS c MATCH (s:Step)-[:INVOLVES]->(c) RETURN DISTINCT s } AS steps
RETURN
  [c IN concepts | {concept: c.name, definition: c.definition,
     aligned_with: COLLECT { MATCH (c)-[:ALIGNED_WITH]->(s:StandardTerm) RETURN s.standard + ': ' + s.term },
     related: COLLECT { MATCH (c)-[r]-(o:Concept) WHERE r.domain
                        RETURN DISTINCT startNode(r).name + ' -' + type(r) + '-> ' + endNode(r).name }}] AS concepts,
  [d IN dps | {data_product: d.name, status: d.status, owner: COLLECT { MATCH (t:Team)-[:OWNS]->(d) RETURN t.name }}] AS data_products,
  [t IN tabs | {table: t.fq_name, platform: t.platform, status: t.status, description: left(t.description, 160),
     hits: size([c IN concepts WHERE EXISTS { (c)-[:MAPPED_TO]->(t) } OR EXISTS { (c)-[:MAPPED_TO]->(:Column)<-[:HAS_COLUMN]-(t) }]),
     columns: COLLECT { MATCH (t)-[:HAS_COLUMN]->(c:Column) RETURN c.name + coalesce(': ' + left(c.description, 60), '') }}] AS tables,
  [m IN mets | {metric: m.name, status: m.status, description: left(m.description, 200),
     expression: COLLECT { MATCH (m)-[:HAS_EXPRESSION]->(e:Expression) RETURN e.expression },
     computed_from: COLLECT { MATCH (m)-[:COMPUTED_FROM]->(c:Column)<-[:HAS_COLUMN]-(t:Table) RETURN t.fq_name + '.' + c.name },
     used_in_reports: COLLECT { MATCH (m)-[:USED_IN]->(r:Report) RETURN r.name },
     variants: COLLECT { MATCH (m)-[:VARIANT_OF]-(v:Metric) RETURN v.name + ' [' + coalesce(v.status, '') + ']' }}] AS metrics,
  [j IN jps | {join_path: j.name, description: j.description, transform: j.transform, max_depth: j.max_depth,
     steps: COLLECT { MATCH (j)-[s:STEP]->(c:Column)<-[:HAS_COLUMN]-(t:Table) RETURN t.fq_name + '.' + c.name ORDER BY s.order }}] AS join_paths,
  [b IN rules | {rule: b.id, name: b.name, text: b.text}] AS business_rules,
  [s IN steps | {process: s.process, step: s.name, order: s.order, description: s.description}] AS process_steps,
  COLLECT { MATCH (t:Table) WHERE t.status IN ['deprecated', 'sandbox']
            RETURN {table: t.fq_name, status: t.status, use_instead: t.replaced_by} } AS deprecated_tables,
  past AS similar_past_answers

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (SELECT p.ACCOUNT_ID, SUM(x.TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY x JOIN wk ON x.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
 JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=x.PRSCRBR_ME
 WHERE x.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') GROUP BY 1),
h AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, pa.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) top_id
 FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT pa ON pa.ACCOUNT_ID=a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
 LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON gp.ACCOUNT_ID=pa.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT h.top_id, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.ACCT_TYP, t.STATE top_state, SUM(rx.trx) trx_13w, COUNT(DISTINCT h.ACCOUNT_ID) n_child_accts,
 (SELECT MIN(WK_END_DT) FROM wk) wk_from, (SELECT MAX(WK_END_DT) FROM wk) wk_to,
 SUM(SUM(rx.trx)) OVER () total_east

reasoning:
I'm verifying the east total of 5,170 matches the earlier figure, and noting which HQs serve which regions — Riverbend is CA-based but its east clinics route through DC-EAST, while Stonegate and Willow Creek are MN-based with east clinics too. Independent clinics like Sunridge Vision Associates 20 don't inherit tier status from similarly-named chains. Now I'm starting the allocation with Riverbend as Tier A at 836.

Adding Oak Hollow and Northfield to complete Tier A at 2,077 (40.2%), then Clearview and Sunridge as Tier B totaling 958 (18.5%), leaving 2,135 (41.3%) for pro-rata distribution among the remaining clinics. I'm computing each clinic's share and running a cumulative sum to make sure the individual allocations add up correctly to the total.

Now I'm checking weekly demand against DC-EAST's shipping rate — about 363 units/week flowing out versus 398 TRx/wk of demand, noting units and TRx aren't equivalent measures. The remaining 80 units from the 9/25 shipment are likely already consumed, meaning there's effectively nothing left at DC-EAST during the gap period, so allocation will need to focus on the next incoming units or an approved transfer. I'm looking at DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST's excess inventory above safety stock levels for FG-1001 and FG-1002 to see if a transfer could help cover the shortfall, though I need to check whether those DCs can spare the stock themselves.

But these DCs also face the same RM-221 delay affecting their own resupply, so pulling from their excess would leave them exposed too — the excess only covers roughly 2-4 weeks of DC-EAST's demand. Calculating days-of-supply for Central and West, I'm realizing that if recovery doesn't happen until around 12/10 (about 71 days out), both Central and West will themselves run out of stock before resupply arrives, with FG-1001 and FG-1002 stockouts projected across late October and early November at each location.

That said, I should be careful not to overstate the risk — Central's inventory is clearly being replenished (falling from 759 to 677 over seven weeks while shipping ~150/week), so it's not identical to DC-EAST's situation. I'll frame transfers as a possible option but caveat it given the shared supplier constraint, and note the DC-EAST stockout predates the late PO rather than being directly caused by it.

Working out the DC-EAST timeline: with 46 and 34 units left and days-of-supply around 1.3 and 2.3, the two SKUs would run out roughly 9/26-28, meaning by the 9/30 data date the DC is already stocked out — the delayed PO doesn't change that stockout date, it just extends the recovery gap. For recovery, PO005791's 4,200 units were promised for 10/07 but shipped late on 10/21 (a 14-day delay... I need to recheck the +50 days figure), pushing arrival to around 12/10 versus an on-time 11/26, creating roughly a 74-day gap from stockout to restock.

I'm also checking whether other POs could arrive sooner — PO000369 is a later-order planned PO promised 10/29 that wouldn't beat the delayed shipment, and I want to verify whether earlier-shipped POs (9/22, 9/24) are already in transit and could reach the DC before PO005791 does, which would shorten the actual outage.

But the rule here is that supply only recovers at the DC once every downstream stage completes, so the intended answer is likely 10/21 + 50 = 12/10. Still, those earlier POs shipped 9/9-9/24 (10,400 units total) could in principle land sooner if dedicated to Lacrivia and DC-EAST specifically, though I can't verify plant WIP allocation since RM-221 also feeds 11 other lens care FGs and Cyclosporine OS. I'll present 12/10 as the planning answer per the question's framing, with a caveat about the earlier pipeline.

That puts the gap from 9/27 to the 12/10 restock at 74 days, versus 60 days if things had gone on-time by 11/26, and I'm now working out the lost demand from that gap.
text:
**Answer: DC-EAST has already run out of Lacrivia, around 26–27 Sep 2026. A two-week slip on S-104's next RM-221 shipment does not change that date. It pushes recovery at DC-EAST from about 26 Nov to about 10 Dec 2026, so the outage lasts about 74 days instead of 60. When supply comes back, the first units go to the three Tier A health systems (Riverbend, Oak Hollow, Northfield), then the two Tier B systems (Clearview, Sunridge), then everyone else pro rata by their prescriptions.**

**1. When DC-EAST runs out** (latest stock count 2026-09-25; days of supply = units on hand ÷ average daily units shipped over the last 28 days)

| Pack | On hand | Safety stock | Avg units shipped/day | Days of supply | Runs out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001) | 46 | 471 | 36.7 | 1.3 | ~26 Sep |
| Lacrivia 10 mL (FG-1002) | 34 | 233 | 15.1 | 2.3 | ~27 Sep |

- Stock fell from about 1,227 and 572 units in mid-August to near zero, which means DC-EAST has had almost no inbound supply for weeks.
- DC-CENTRAL (677 / 351 units) and DC-WEST (593 / 324 units) are still above safety stock.

**2. When supply recovers**
- **The shipment:** the next one is PO005791, 4,200 units of RM-221, still open, with a promised ship date of 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships 21 Oct.
- **RM-221 has no backup supplier.** S-104 is the only qualified source; S-131 is not qualified. The premix it goes into (CMP-310) also has a single supplier, S-201.
- **Lead time from S-104 shipping to finished goods at the DC is 50 days, using standard factory times:**
  - Transit from S-104 to S-201: 6 days
  - Premix (CMP-310), including transit to plant PL-01: 10 days
  - First bulk stage (SEMI-031): 4 days
  - Second bulk stage (SEMI-044): 8 days
  - Filling: 3 days
  - Finishing and QC release, including the 14-day sterility test: 15 days
  - Transit to the DC: 4 days
- **Recovery date:** 21 Oct + 50 days = **about 10 Dec 2026**. If the shipment were on time, it would be about 26 Nov.
- **Impact:** the delay adds 14 days of outage, about 725 units of DC-EAST demand. Across the whole gap, about 3,800 units of demand go unfilled.

**3. Who gets supply first** (our allocation rule; customers are the top-level health system, or the clinic itself if independent; prescriptions are the last 13 weeks, 3 Jul to 25 Sep, Lacrivia written by prescribers at clinics in DC-EAST's states)

| Priority | Customer | Prescriptions | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 – Tier A | Riverbend Health System | 836 | |
| 1 – Tier A | Oak Hollow Health System | 708 | |
| 1 – Tier A | Northfield Health System | 533 | 2,077 total (40%) |
| 2 – Tier B | Clearview Health System | 530 | |
| 2 – Tier B | Sunridge Health System | 428 | 958 total (19%) |
| 3 – Pro rata | All others | 2,135 total (41%) | Brightwater HS 19.4%, Stonegate HS 15.0%, Sunridge Vision Assoc. 20 9.3%, Willow Creek HS 8.8%, Harbor Point VA 2 6.5%, Highland VA 26 6.2%, then 12 smaller independent clinics |

- Clinics get the contract tier of the health system they belong to.
- Some independent clinics have similar names to contracted systems (for example Sunridge Vision Associates 20). They have no parent in the account data, so they do not get Sunridge's Tier B priority.
- Riverbend, Stonegate and Willow Creek are headquartered outside the East. Only their East-state clinics count here.
- The Tier A systems alone write about 160 prescriptions a week. The first recovered lots will go almost entirely to Tier A and Tier B before pro-rata customers get any.

**Options and cautions**
- **No company substitute.** The approved substitute, Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003), is made from the same RM-221 and premix. DC-EAST does hold 615 units of it, but under our substitute rule there is no approved company substitute here, so Medical Affairs should guide therapeutic alternatives.
- **Stock transfers.** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold about 695 units of 5 mL and 391 units of 10 mL above safety stock, roughly 19–26 days of DC-EAST demand. Moving any of it needs Supply Planning approval. Those DCs also depend on RM-221, so check their own runway against a 10 Dec recovery first.
- **Earlier shipments might arrive sooner.** RM-221 shipped on 9–24 Sep (PO000362/363/364, about 10,400 units) could reach the DC from late October if it is committed to Lacrivia. I can't see factory work-in-progress (PLANT_MATERIAL only maps plants to materials), so please confirm with the MES / plant schedule. RM-221 also feeds Cyclosporine OS and 11 lens-care products.

**Sources and assumptions**
- **Tools:** `get_context` (shortage allocation, recovery lead time, substitutes, customer definition and DC service-region rules; days-of-supply metric), `trace_supply_exposure` (S-104 / RM-221), `get_lead_times` (RM-221 to FG-1001 and FG-1002).
- **Reference data:** `supply_contracts` (contract tiers) and `dc_service_regions` (DC-EAST serves NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC, OH).
- **Fabric tables:** dbo.PURCH_ORD, dbo.DC_INV, dbo.WHSLR_SHIP.
- **Snowflake tables:** RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY (Lacrivia NDCs 99101010105 and 99101010110), CORE.PRESCRIBER, CORE.ACCOUNT (clinics rolled up two levels to the top account).
- **Past answer:** this builds on the earlier "DC-EAST Lacrivia stockout risk" analysis. Its numbers match (5,170 prescriptions; 46 / 34 units on hand).
- **Assumptions:**
  - "Next shipment" means PO005791. PO000369 is dated after the data date and is promised later.
  - The 50-day lead time starts when S-104 ships.
  - No unrecorded receipts arrived at DC-EAST after 25 Sep.
  - Allocation uses last-13-week prescriptions as written, not wholesaler orders.

                    RETURN n LIMIT 1
                    UNION
                    MATCH (n:Table) WHERE toUpper(n.fq_name) = toUpper(nm) OR toUpper(n.fq_name) ENDS WITH '.' + toUpper(nm)
                    RETURN n LIMIT 1 }
                  MERGE (d)-[:USED]->(n) RETURN collect(DISTINCT coalesce(n.fq_name, n.name)) AS linked

question: If S-104's next RM-221 shipment ships two weeks late, when will DC-EAST run out of Lacrivia, when will supply recover there, and which customers get supply first under our allocation rules?
answer:
**Answer: DC-EAST has already run out of Lacrivia, around 26–27 Sep 2026. A two-week slip on S-104's next RM-221 shipment does not change that date. It pushes recovery at DC-EAST from about 26 Nov to about 10 Dec 2026, so the outage lasts about 74 days instead of 60. When supply comes back, the first units go to the three Tier A health systems (Riverbend, Oak Hollow, Northfield), then the two Tier B systems (Clearview, Sunridge), then everyone else pro rata by their prescriptions.**

**1. When DC-EAST runs out** (latest stock count 2026-09-25; days of supply = units on hand ÷ average daily units shipped over the last 28 days)

| Pack | On hand | Safety stock | Avg units shipped/day | Days of supply | Runs out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL (FG-1001) | 46 | 471 | 36.7 | 1.3 | ~26 Sep |
| Lacrivia 10 mL (FG-1002) | 34 | 233 | 15.1 | 2.3 | ~27 Sep |

- Stock fell from about 1,227 and 572 units in mid-August to near zero, which means DC-EAST has had almost no inbound supply for weeks.
- DC-CENTRAL (677 / 351 units) and DC-WEST (593 / 324 units) are still above safety stock.

**2. When supply recovers**
- **The shipment:** the next one is PO005791, 4,200 units of RM-221, still open, with a promised ship date of 7 Oct. Two weeks late means it ships 21 Oct.
- **RM-221 has no backup supplier.** S-104 is the only qualified source; S-131 is not qualified. The premix it goes into (CMP-310) also has a single supplier, S-201.
- **Lead time from S-104 shipping to finished goods at the DC is 50 days, using standard factory times:**
  - Transit from S-104 to S-201: 6 days
  - Premix (CMP-310), including transit to plant PL-01: 10 days
  - First bulk stage (SEMI-031): 4 days
  - Second bulk stage (SEMI-044): 8 days
  - Filling: 3 days
  - Finishing and QC release, including the 14-day sterility test: 15 days
  - Transit to the DC: 4 days
- **Recovery date:** 21 Oct + 50 days = **about 10 Dec 2026**. If the shipment were on time, it would be about 26 Nov.
- **Impact:** the delay adds 14 days of outage, about 725 units of DC-EAST demand. Across the whole gap, about 3,800 units of demand go unfilled.

**3. Who gets supply first** (our allocation rule; customers are the top-level health system, or the clinic itself if independent; prescriptions are the last 13 weeks, 3 Jul to 25 Sep, Lacrivia written by prescribers at clinics in DC-EAST's states)

| Priority | Customer | Prescriptions | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 – Tier A | Riverbend Health System | 836 | |
| 1 – Tier A | Oak Hollow Health System | 708 | |
| 1 – Tier A | Northfield Health System | 533 | 2,077 total (40%) |
| 2 – Tier B | Clearview Health System | 530 | |
| 2 – Tier B | Sunridge Health System | 428 | 958 total (19%) |
| 3 – Pro rata | All others | 2,135 total (41%) | Brightwater HS 19.4%, Stonegate HS 15.0%, Sunridge Vision Assoc. 20 9.3%, Willow Creek HS 8.8%, Harbor Point VA 2 6.5%, Highland VA 26 6.2%, then 12 smaller independent clinics |

- Clinics get the contract tier of the health system they belong to.
- Some independent clinics have similar names to contracted systems (for example Sunridge Vision Associates 20). They have no parent in the account data, so they do not get Sunridge's Tier B priority.
- Riverbend, Stonegate and Willow Creek are headquartered outside the East. Only their East-state clinics count here.
- The Tier A systems alone write about 160 prescriptions a week. The first recovered lots will go almost entirely to Tier A and Tier B before pro-rata customers get any.

**Options and cautions**
- **No company substitute.** The approved substitute, Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003), is made from the same RM-221 and premix. DC-EAST does hold 615 units of it, but under our substitute rule there is no approved company substitute here, so Medical Affairs should guide therapeutic alternatives.
- **Stock transfers.** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold about 695 units of 5 mL and 391 units of 10 mL above safety stock, roughly 19–26 days of DC-EAST demand. Moving any of it needs Supply Planning approval. Those DCs also depend on RM-221, so check their own runway against a 10 Dec recovery first.
- **Earlier shipments might arrive sooner.** RM-221 shipped on 9–24 Sep (PO000362/363/364, about 10,400 units) could reach the DC from late October if it is committed to Lacrivia. I can't see factory work-in-progress (PLANT_MATERIAL only maps plants to materials), so please confirm with the MES / plant schedule. RM-221 also feeds Cyclosporine OS and 11 lens-care products.

**Sources and assumptions**
- **Tools:** `get_context` (shortage allocation, recovery lead time, substitutes, customer definition and DC service-region rules; days-of-supply metric), `trace_supply_exposure` (S-104 / RM-221), `get_lead_times` (RM-221 to FG-1001 and FG-1002).
- **Reference data:** `supply_contracts` (contract tiers) and `dc_service_regions` (DC-EAST serves NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC, OH).
- **Fabric tables:** dbo.PURCH_ORD, dbo.DC_INV, dbo.WHSLR_SHIP.
- **Snowflake tables:** RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY (Lacrivia NDCs 99101010105 and 99101010110), CORE.PRESCRIBER, CORE.ACCOUNT (clinics rolled up two levels to the top account).
- **Past answer:** this builds on the earlier "DC-EAST Lacrivia stockout risk" analysis. Its numbers match (5,170 prescriptions; 46 / 34 units on hand).
- **Assumptions:**
  - "Next shipment" means PO005791. PO000369 is dated after the data date and is promised later.
  - The 50-day lead time starts when S-104 ships.
  - No unrecorded receipts arrived at DC-EAST after 25 Sep.
  - Allocation uses last-13-week prescriptions as written, not wholesaler orders.

sql.sql: SELECT PO_ID, SUPPLIER_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND MATERIAL_ID='RM-221' ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT DESC

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT, ON_HAND_UNITS, SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND SNAPSHOT_DT >= '2026-08-01' ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID, SNAPSHOT_DT

SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, SUM(UNITS) AS units_28d, SUM(UNITS)/28.0 AS avg_daily, MIN(SHIP_DT) mn, MAX(SHIP_DT) mx FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,'2026-09-30') AND SHIP_DT <= '2026-09-30' GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY MATERIAL_ID, DC_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (SELECT p.ACCOUNT_ID, SUM(x.TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY x JOIN wk ON x.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
 JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=x.PRSCRBR_ME
 WHERE x.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') GROUP BY 1),
h AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, pa.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) top_id
 FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT pa ON pa.ACCOUNT_ID=a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
 LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON gp.ACCOUNT_ID=pa.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT h.top_id, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.ACCT_TYP, t.STATE top_state, SUM(rx.trx) trx_13w, COUNT(DISTINCT h.ACCOUNT_ID) n_child_accts,
 (SELECT MIN(WK_END_DT) FROM wk) wk_from, (SELECT MAX(WK_END_DT) FROM wk) wk_to,
 SUM(SUM(rx.trx)) OVER () total_east
FROM rx JOIN h ON h.ACCOUNT_ID=rx.ACCOUNT_ID JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=h.top_id
WHERE h.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY trx_13w DESC LIMIT 40
